subject: Problem recapturing values from simulated data

messages.author: 1c8f850916760249
messages.subject: Problem recapturing values from simulated data
parts:
Hi all —


I’m working on a hierarchical model of timing of leafout for trees, could use help figuring out why my fitted values differ so much from my (simulated) data in some simple parameters. I don’t know exactly where I went wrong in the model specification, so could use some help from this group.


The set up is that I have multiple species, and within species I have multiple individual trees. Each tree has branches taken from it and exposed to different experimental conditions; we measure day of leaf expansion. So there are random intercepts at the species and tree level, and random slopes as well for the effects of the experimental conditions.


I’m generating simulated data to test the model with an overall day of leafout of 35 days, then variation around that for species-level intercepts, and variation around each of those at the individual level. I'm not simulating variation of the slopes at species or individual level.


The surprising thing is that the fitted values come up with an overall day of leafout (“a_0” in the model) of 70 days. All the other intercepts at the species and individual level vary the way I expect, but around this higher value. The slopes follow the simulated values well. 


My problem is in figuring out why the fitted intercepts are so high, and here I’m hoping this group can help me! I’m attaching the stan model, as well as a figure from a posterior predictive check, showing the shift in intercept up for the fitted values, and associated R code for those interested.


Any thoughts would be most welcome!


Dan

messages.author: e66baf722e0aed3f
messages.subject: Re: Problem recapturing values from simulated data
parts:
Hi there, Dan.

I didn't run all the way through your code - but I did notice the following line:

# Make a lookup vector for which species each individual tree belongs to
splookup <- unique(fake[c("ind","sp")])[,"sp"] #200 long = 10 ind x 20 sp

Are you certain that this lookup works?

I ask only because depending on whether or not your data are sorted, the unique vector may not work -- I have found that it is sometimes necessary to ensure the data are ordered, and I often use a sort function when using lookups... I found this out the hard way when I was trying to fit a fairly simple model, and similarly my intercepts were off and in my case my fixed effects were all suppressed. Basically - my lookup didn't work (I needed to sort according to the lower-level index value) - and so I was trying to fit a misspecified model!

This isn't Stan specific, necessarily - but maybe it helps :)

Good luck!
S

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Problem recapturing values from simulated data
parts:
My guess is that your use of the non-centered mean is
not getting adjusted for properly in the comparison.

// a_0 should end up ~ 35, getting 65 days instead!

Did you mean a_sp here?

y_hat[i] <- a_sp_ind[ind[i]] +
b_warm_sp_ind[ind[i]] * warm[i] +
b_photo_sp_ind[ind[i]] * photo[i]
;

a_sp[k] <- a_0 + mu_a_sp[k];

This bit's not identified. You can add a constant to a_0
and subtract it from all the mu_a_sp and get the same result.
Given that you let the scale of mu_a_sp vary:

mu_a_sp ~ normal(0, sigma_a_sp);

and don't provide any prior whatsoever for a_0, this can
be a problem. I'd check that you're recovering the a_sp
properly given that the a_0 isn't identified.

We always suggest starting simpler and building up models.
It's much harder to debug a complicated model than to build
up a simpler model a step at a time.

Another think to look at is whether your y_hat is right. If
it is, but the components don't do what you think, it's probably
an identifiability problem.

- Bob
